themes.topic: Eclipse as ritual trigger for obligatory rites

mentions.quote: One should bathe at an eclipse of the moon and sun, and also during a period of birth or death impurity.
And at an eclipse (uparāge), an ancestral rite (śrāddham) is obligatory.
Giving (dānam) is also obligatory.

themes.justification: The entire window is structured around the eclipse (grahaṇa/uparāga) as the occasion that makes bathing, śrāddha, and giving legally obligatory — this is the organizing principle of this section of the Vīramitrodaya.

themes.justification: A central theme of the window is the ranking of water sources — from drawn water to rivers, with the Gaṅgā at the apex — and of tīrthas, with month-specific and eclipse-type-specific hierarchies derived from multiple Purāṇas.

themes.topic: Ritual impurity (sūtaka) at eclipse and its scope

mentions.quote: Impurity (āśaucaṃ) arises for men (nṝṇāṃ) at an eclipse of the moon and sun.
For all social classes, there is ritual impurity (sūtakaṃ) at the sight of Rāhu (Rāhu).
At an eclipse, the impurity is like that of a corpse (śāvamāśaucaṃ); at liberation, it is remembered as like that of birth (sautikaṃ).

themes.justification: The text extensively analyzes the nature and scope of eclipse-related impurity — comparing it to corpse and birth impurity, determining that it applies universally to all four varṇas, and specifying when purity is restored.

themes.topic: Dialectical engagement with divergent smṛti authorities

mentions.quote: By this, the view of Jīmūtavāhana, that in a period of impurity at an eclipse, only bathing should be performed, not giving, ancestral rites, etc., is refuted.
By this, the view of the Madanaratna, that only the bathing at liberation is with clothes on, is refuted.
In reality, it is without foundation, because it is not written in the Prayogapārijāta, and because 'devoid of giving and ancestral rites' is redundant.

themes.justification: The Vīramitrodaya consistently positions itself against rival digest traditions (Jīmūtavāhana, Madanaratna, Saṃvatsarapradīpa), explicitly refuting their positions — a characteristic of its genre as a polemical digest.

citations.quote: This is from the Mātsya Purāṇa.
citations.justification: The Mātsya Purāṇa is also cited as authority for the rule that eclipse rites should be performed even in an intercalary month.

citations.quote: Concerning the ancestral rite (śrāddhaṃ), in the Kūrma Purāṇa also: An occasional (naimittikaṃ) rite should be performed at an eclipse of the moon and sun
citations.justification: The Kūrma Purāṇa is cited as a corroborating authority that the eclipse śrāddha is an obligatory occasional rite.

citations.quote: This is from the Vāyu Purāṇa.
citations.justification: The Vāyu Purāṇa is cited as authority for the rule that śrāddha should be avoided at night except for Rāhu (eclipse) and periods of impurity.

citations.quote: From this statement in the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, which states the impurity of a corpse and of birth at the contact and liberation
citations.justification: The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is cited as authority for distinguishing corpse-impurity (at eclipse contact) from birth-impurity (at liberation), with implications for bathing procedure.

citations.quote: This is from the Brahmavaivarta.
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta is cited for the sequence: bathing → homa → śrāddha, establishing the ritual order for eclipse rites.

citations.quote: And what is in the Brahmavaivarta cited by Hemādri: At an eclipse of the moon and sun, one should not eat for the first four yāmas.
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta (via Hemādri) is cited as authority on the number of yāmas before an eclipse during which eating is prohibited.

citations.quote: In the Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa: Cows, elephants (nāgāḥ), sesame seeds (tilā), grain (dhānyaṃ), gems (ratnāni), gold (kanakaṃ), and
citations.justification: The Prabhāsa Khaṇḍa is cited for a list of meritorious gifts given at the Cūḍāmaṇi yoga eclipse, expanding the eclipse giving injunction.

citations.quote: In the Skānda Purāṇa cited by Mādhava: When a lunar eclipse is after midnight, one should eat in the forenoon, never at midday.
citations.justification: The Skānda Purāṇa (via Mādhava) is cited for detailed temporal rules on eating after a lunar eclipse that crosses midnight.

citations.quote: In the Śivarahasya: As long as the eclipse of the sun and moon lasts, one should perform recitation (japa), etc.
citations.justification: The Śivarahasya is cited as authority for the general prohibition on sleeping and eating during the eclipse, with the injunction to perform japa throughout.

citations.quote: from the mention of 'according to the rules,' what is said in the Smṛtiratnāvalī, 'this bathing is without mantras,' is refuted.
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya explicitly refutes the Smṛtiratnāvalī's view that eclipse bathing is performed without mantras, using the Mahābhārata's phrase 'according to the rules' as counter-evidence.

citations.quote: The procedure for bathing is in the Mitākṣarā:
citations.justification: The Mitākṣarā (the famous Vijñāneśvara commentary on the Yājñavalkyasmṛti) is cited for the procedure of bathing for menstruating women during an obligatory eclipse occasion.

citations.quote: What is left over in new ancestral rites, and what has been kept overnight (paryuṣitaṃ) at an eclipse, from a smṛti in the Mitākṣarā.
citations.justification: The Mitākṣarā is cited again as the source for a smṛti statement that food kept overnight from an eclipse must be discarded.

citations.quote: In the Kālādarśa, however, after the verse 'When the eclipse of the moon is,' the following verse is also read under the name of Vasiṣṭha:
citations.justification: The Kālādarśa is cited as the source-text that transmits a Vasiṣṭha verse on the timing of eating permitted during eclipse, used in the Vīramitrodaya's arbitration.

citations.quote: In the Kālādarśa also:
citations.justification: The Kālādarśa is cited a second time for a Gārgya verse on prohibition of eating when eclipses occur at twilight.

citations.quote: When the annual ancestral rite (pratyābdika) falls on that day, in the Madanapārijāta:
citations.justification: The Madanapārijāta is cited as the digest-text transmitting Gohila's ruling on the annual śrāddha falling on an eclipse day.

citations.quote: And because it contradicts the statement written in the Kālādarśa, Madanapārijāta, and Candraprakāśa.
citations.justification: The Madanapārijāta is cited along with the Kālādarśa and Candraprakāśa as a digest that the Vīramitrodaya appeals to against Jīmūtavāhana's restricted view.

citations.quote: By this, the view of the Madanaratna, that only the bathing at liberation is with clothes on, is refuted.
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya explicitly refutes the Madanaratna's narrow view that clothed bathing applies only at eclipse liberation, arguing it applies at contact as well.

citations.quote: This is from another smṛti stated in the Candraprakāśa.
citations.justification: The Candraprakāśa is cited as the transmitting digest-text for a smṛti on the ritual sequence (bathing → breath control → libations → homa → śrāddha) at eclipses.

citations.quote: And because it contradicts the statement written in the Kālādarśa, Madanapārijāta, and Candraprakāśa.
citations.justification: The Candraprakāśa is cited alongside the Kālādarśa and Madanapārijāta as supporting the broader view of eclipse rites against Jīmūtavāhana.

citations.quote: Likewise in the Pṛthvīcandrodaya, Nirṇayāmṛta, and Prayogapārijāta.
citations.justification: The Pṛthvīcandrodaya is listed alongside two other digests as corroborating the ruling that annual śrāddha should be performed on the eclipse day itself.

citations.quote: Likewise in the Pṛthvīcandrodaya, Nirṇayāmṛta, and Prayogapārijāta.
citations.justification: The Nirṇayāmṛta is listed as one of three corroborating digest authorities on performing annual śrāddha on the eclipse day.

citations.quote: Likewise in the Pṛthvīcandrodaya, Nirṇayāmṛta, and Prayogapārijāta.
citations.justification: The Prayogapārijāta is one of three digests cited as corroborating the ruling on annual śrāddha at eclipses.

citations.quote: In reality, it is without foundation, because it is not written in the Prayogapārijāta
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya appeals to the Prayogapārijāta's silence to refute an unattested smṛti statement found in the Saṃvatsarapradīpa.

citations.quote: As for the statement in the Saṃvatsarapradīpa, etc.— In a period of birth or death impurity (sūtake mṛtake caiva), there is no fault at the sight of Rāhu. / Only bathing should be performed, devoid of giving and ancestral rites
citations.justification: The Vīramitrodaya cites and then rejects the Saṃvatsarapradīpa's restrictive rule, declaring it without foundation since its source cannot be verified.

citations.quote: The Kalpataru says that the four muhūrtas after one and a half praharas (watches) is the mahāniśā.
citations.justification: The Kalpataru (a dharmaśāstra digest) is cited as an alternative authority defining the mahāniśā, giving a different reading from Mārkaṇḍeya's definition.

citations.quote: A penance for eating at the time of an eclipse and during its conjunction is stated by Kātyāyana in the Mādhavīya:
citations.justification: The Mādhavīya (Mādhava's commentary or digest) is cited as the text that transmits Kātyāyana's ruling on penance for eclipse-time eating violations.

citations.quote: This is from a statement of the Sūryodaya-nibandha in the Bhārgavārcanadīpikā.
citations.justification: The Bhārgavārcanadīpikā is cited as the digest transmitting the Sūryodaya-nibandha's ruling that menstruating women may bathe from a distance using drawn water during an eclipse.

citations.quote: This is also from the Ṣaṭtriṃśanmata.
citations.justification: The Ṣaḍtriṃśanmata is cited as authority for the rule that all social classes have eclipse impurity (sūtaka) and must bathe to regain eligibility for rites.

citations.quote: The definition of a Brahmin in name only (viprabruva) is in the Ṣaḍtriṃśanmata:
citations.justification: The Ṣaḍtriṃśanmata is also cited for the definition of a 'Brahmin in name only' relevant to determining eligible gift recipients during eclipses.

citations.quote: This is from the Caturviṃśatimata.
citations.justification: The Caturviṃśatimata is cited as the source for a verse defining 'Brahmin by birth alone' as those who know only the Gāyatrī and perform the twilight prayer.

citations.quote: The reading in the Kālamādhava, however, is gāṃ harīśāṅghikāt.
citations.justification: The Kālamādhava is cited in a textual note as offering an alternate reading of a verse, indicating that the Vīramitrodaya is aware of variant manuscript readings.
